subject: Re: Indemnity scope rationalization & evidence template
messages:
From: Laura Dunn <laura.dunn@novahealth.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Rivera <mrivera@novalegal.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity ask re: model-output IP claims

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — we’re excited about how Redwood is performing on our product flows. Our in-house counsel asked me to follow up on indemnity language in the MSA and a couple of related Order Form points. Two specific asks:

1) We need Redwood to cover third-party IP claims that arise from content the model generates (we've seen this in the market).
2) We need a clear evidence/notice protocol so our security/legal ops team can respond quickly if a claim arrives.

Attached is an anonymized complaint (Nova_complaint_sample.pdf) to show the sort of allegations we want covered. Can you share Redwood’s proposed redlines and an evidence checklist for triage? Ben — looping you in on timeline and SLA questions.

Best,
Laura
Laura Dunn
Head of Corporate Counsel, NovaHealth AI
laura.dunn@novahealth.ai

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Dunn <laura.dunn@novahealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask re: model-output IP claims

Hi Laura — thanks for the note and the sample complaint, that’s helpful context. Quick summary of where we think we can land and open items to resolve with legal: 

- Redwood position (high level): We can provide indemnity for third-party IP claims to the extent they arise from model outputs provided via the Redwood service, subject to limited carveouts (open-source components, third-party data sources, and customer-provided prompts/content), a reasonable cap tied to the Order Form value, and typical procedures for notice and cooperation.
- Evidence / notice protocol: we propose a 30-day notice window for claims (from the date of written notice), an evidence handback template (attached: evidence_handback_template.xlsx), and a named technical liaison for triage.
- Defense control: Redwood prefers to defend with Redwood-selected counsel for tech/IP claims, but we are open to a joint-defense approach for sensitive settlements.
- Insurance interplay: we propose an insurer-offset clause (so available insurance proceeds offset Redwood's liability) and request a minimum insurance representation from Nova (cyber/tech E&O with a $5M limit).

I’ve attached our proposed redlines (Redwood_proposed_redlines_20270903.docx). Kimberly, can you review the redline highlights below and flag any negotiation points we should expect? Ben — Laura asked about SLA/timing; can you recommend the commercial levers (cap $ vs. term, premium, dedicated capacity) we can offer to move acceptance?

Next step: propose a 30-minute legal-only sync with Nova counsel early next week, then a joint call if needed.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O’Connor
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Dunn <laura.dunn@novahealth.ai>, Mark Rivera <mrivera@novalegal.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask re: model-output IP claims

Grace / team — drafting notes and negotiation playbook below. I also attached a compact evidence checklist in the redlines doc and included language suggestions. Key points: 

1) Scope carveouts (we should hold):
   - Open-source components where the OSS license requires different indemnity obligations.
   - Third-party data/content that Nova supplies (customer prompts, proprietary training data identified by Nova).
   - Content generated by models not validated/approved by Redwood where Nova materially modified model prompts or post-processing.

2) Defense vs. indemnity mechanics:
   - Redwood will defend and indemnify for third-party IP claims "to the extent caused by the service output".
   - Require notice within 30 days and reasonable cooperation; Redwood must be given primary control to select counsel (Redwood may choose outside counsel with appropriate expertise).
   - Settlement consent: customer cannot settle in a way that imposes obligations on Redwood without Redwood's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).

3) Caps, insurance, and offsets:
   - Proposed cap: we suggest a multiple of 12 months of charges under the Order Form (or a fixed $2M floor for SMB deals, escalate for enterprise).
   - Insurance offset: Redwood requests that available insurance proceeds be applied to indemnity so Redwood liability is reduced by amounts payable under Nova's insurance.
   - We will accept insurer-offset language but push back on full elimination of cap by insurer proceeds — counterproposal: cap reduced but not eliminated where insurance exists (details in redlines).

4) Evidence and triage timeline:
   - Evidence package: complaint, sample prompt (if available), example output, server logs for request id(s), and a short technical summary from Nova’s ops team.
   - We propose a 5-business-day acknowledgement SLA and a 15-business-day preliminary tech review window to determine plausibility and scope for remediation.

5) Optional commercial mitigations to offer Nova:
   - Increased monitoring/alerting add-on and dedicated capacity with pre-approved model variants (reduces risk).
   - Escrow for high-dollar deals or express insurance placement assistance.

Ben — commercial to confirm what level of cap/credits will move the deal. Laura / Mark — happy to discuss these tradeoffs on a call next week.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Mark Rivera <mrivera@novalegal.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Dunn <laura.dunn@novahealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask re: model-output IP claims

Kimberly / Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few counters from Nova’s side: 

- Cap: we cannot accept a cap that is effectively reduced to nothing by insurance offsets. For enterprise deals we typically ask for a standalone indemnity cap that is meaningful (we suggest 3x ARR or a floor of $5M).
- Defense control: we prefer litigation control to be with the defending party; however, we expect reasonable settlement approval rights. The "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard is OK, but we need clarity on timing for consent.
- Evidence: the evidence checklist looks good. We will not provide raw customer prompts without a narrow subpoena protection and redaction process; we need Redwood to accept sanitized examples when available.

I propose the following compromise: standalone indemnity cap of $5M for this Order Form, Redwood retains defense control but provides a 10-business-day window for Nova to review and raise objections to settlement terms; insurer proceeds reduce Redwood’s payment but not below 50% of the cap. If Redwood can sign to that, I think we can move to contract execution quickly.

On a practical note: the complaint attached is an older case — Nova has also seen model-output allegations tied to 3rd party content providers. Would Redwood accept a limited subrogation right to pursue the upstream provider if we agree to evidence transfer protocols?

Thanks,
Mark

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Rivera <mrivera@novalegal.com>, Laura Dunn <laura.dunn@novahealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask re: model-output IP claims

Mark / Laura — appreciate the constructive counterproposal. Internal takeaways and next steps: 

- Commercial compromise: Ben will propose a commercial package to bridge to a $5M floor for this Order Form (combo of slight price premium + 12‑month committed capacity).
- Legal compromise: Kimberly is comfortable with Redwood retaining primary defense control provided Nova has a 10-business-day review for settlements and insurer-offset cannot reduce Redwood’s liability below 50% of the cap (language to be drafted).
- Evidence & subrogation: Redwood agrees in principle to a limited subrogation right where upstream provider attribution is proven with logs; we’ll need a narrow process for sanitized prompt sharing and NDAs.

Action items:
- Ben: share commercial offer and revised Order Form terms by Fri 9 Sep.
- Kimberly: update redlines to reflect the 10-business-day settlement review, the 50% insurer floor, and narrow subrogation language.
- Laura / Mark: confirm availability for a 30-min call Wed 8 Sep or Thu 9 Sep to finalize language.

I’ve attached the evidence-handback template and our current redlines for the call. Thanks all — I think this is a fast path to close.

Regards,
Grace
